- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ in 30d), especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags — anticipate reversal and adjust forecast upward 1–3 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30d horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is volatile — use 18d average as baseline, then add sentiment-weighted adjustment (e.g., +0.1–0.3 if sentiment >0.6).
